newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa writes letters despite bronchitis.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa writes letters despite bronchitis.

text.p: Mother Teresa on Tuesday answered letters from anxious correspondents all over the globe who had sent their best wishes, but doctors said a persistent respiratory disease would slow her recovery.
However they hoped she would be well enough to go home for Christmas.
The Roman Catholic nun is battling stubborn bronchitis in hospital as she recovers from heart surgery, but had improved enough to sit up and write letters, a panel of doctors said.
"This afternoon she is sitting, writing and answering letters coming from all over the world wishing her a speedy recovery," the doctors at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said.
"(Her) bronchial pneumonia (is) responding to therapy, (with) slight improvement today," they said in a regular bulletin.
Mother Teresa, 86, had had bronchitis for many years, Dr Patricia Aubanel, an American member of the panel, told reporters.
"She has had some bronchitis for a long time and some lung disease for a long time, even when she was a child," Dr Aubanel said. "She's been having bronchitis for the last two months."
Aubanel said the bronchitis germ was a difficult organism to treat. It had built up resistance to many antibiotic drugs given to Mother Teresa during earlier illnesses.
"Finally we found the right antibiotic for her and it seems she's trying to respond," Aubanel told reporters.

"But obviously her lungs are not as strong as they were before. Her lungs are weaker, so it takes a longer time to recuperate, she needs a lot of respiratory therapy, a lot of exercises and we're feeling for her as well," Aubanel added.

Mother Teresa underwent surgery to clear two blocked coronary arteries on November 29. She had appeared to be recovering, despite an irregular heartbeat, when long-standing kidney and lung problems added complications.
Doctors say her kidney function has since returned to normal. Her cardiac status is stable, despite her irregular heartbeat. But her body is fighting hard to shake off the bronchial problems.
Aubanel said the doctors hoped the 1979 Nobel peace prize winner would be well enough to return home for Christmas.
On Tuesday her appetite had improved. Doctors planned to offer her a favourite dish for dinner -- chicken cutlets, a clinic official said.
"She's sleeping well and she's eating well," said administrator A.K. Chatterjee. "Those are good signs."
Doctors said she spent many hours of the day praying.

Mother Teresa has frequently said during the last week that she would like to return to her work among the poor, the sick and the terminally ill as soon as possible, which has earned her the title "Saint of the Gutters".
"When are you sending me home?" a clinic official quoted her as saying on Tuesday. "I'm absolutely all right."
